entries.title: Irish police X accounts hijacked to push a crypto scam
entries.summary: An Garda Síochána (Ireland's police) confirmed unauthorised access to its X accounts @gardainfo and @gardatraffic and warned the public not to interact with anything posted on them, or on accounts pretending to be them. The Irish Times reports @GardaInfo was rebranded to look like a crypto wallet's support account and posted scores of crypto posts. Garda regained control on Oct 15; the accounts stay inactive while the Garda National Cyber Crime Bureau investigates.
entries.lesson: A verified account with a trusted name can still be hijacked. A blue tick is not proof. Never connect a wallet from a post you were tagged in.

entries.title: Ripple: no "XRP Rewards Scanner", no unclaimed XRP via wallet scan
entries.summary: RippleX posted that Ripple is not running an "XRP Rewards Scanner" or offering unclaimed XRP through a wallet scan, and that screenshots claiming otherwise are fake.
entries.lesson: "Scan your wallet for unclaimed XRP" is a scam pattern. Never share your secret key or recovery phrase, and review every transaction before signing.

sources.label: Ripple: how to identify crypto scams

entries.title: Xaman: "We will never issue a token or an airdrop"
entries.summary: Xaman Wallet warned of an ongoing scam wave against XRP holders: it will never DM you, never email you, and never issue a token or an airdrop. Its support exists only inside the Xaman app.
entries.lesson: Any "Xaman airdrop" or Xaman "support" outside the app is fake.
